sections.section_name: Section B - Art Elements & Conceptual Terms

questions.question_text: Explain the meaning and artistic significance of 'Pramanam' as the second core component within the Six Limbs of Indian Painting (Shadang). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Pramanam refers to the correct perception, structural measurement, and accurate proportion of forms. It ensures aesthetic balance, establishing harmonious structural relationships between different anatomical parts within a composition.

questions.question_text: Define the structural element of 'Texture' in visual arts and identify its presence in the Indus Valley terracotta mother goddess figurines. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Texture defines the tactile surface quality of an artwork. In Harappan terracotta mother goddesses, pinched facial features and applied clay ornaments create a distinctively rough, expressive, and unrefined structural texture.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of 'Bhava' within the Six Limbs of Indian Painting (Shadang) and its impact on the viewer. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bhava translates to the expression of deep emotion or mood in an artwork. It imbues static forms with emotional resonance, allowing the painting to evoke specific psychological feelings within the viewer.

questions.question_text: Describe the fundamental technique of 'Tempera' painting as widely observed in the classical murals of the Ajanta caves. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Tempera is a painting technique where natural mineral pigments are bound using an organic water-soluble binder, like animal glue or plant gum, and applied onto a dry mud-plastered wall surface.

questions.question_text: Analyze the expressive function of 'Line' (Rekha) as a core art element in the structural composition of Ajanta paintings. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: In Ajanta, fluid, rhythmic, and sweeping lines define the anatomical contours and lyrical grace of the figures. They structurally establish volume and three-dimensional solidity without relying heavily on harsh shading.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the aesthetic styling, posture dynamics, and casting technique of the bronze 'Dancing Girl' artifact from Mohenjo-Daro. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Cast using the lost-wax (cire-perdue) technique, this four-inch bronze figurine displays a relaxed, tribhanga (three-bend) posture with one hand on her hip. Adorned with a multitude of bangles on her left arm, her stylized, elongated limbs capture a bold, rhythmic vitality and exceptional proto-historic metallurgical skill.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the structural proportions, surface treatment, and volumetric rendering of the 'Didarganj Yakshini' sculpture from the Mauryan period. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Carved from a single piece of Chunar sandstone, the Didarganj Yakshini features the hallmark mirror-like Mauryan polish. The life-size sculpture showcases heavy, rounded volumetric proportions, full breasts, and a narrow waist, epitomizing ancient Indian feminine fertility and exquisite structural detailing in her elaborate drapery and jewelry.

questions.question_text: Analyze the narrative composition, emotional depth, and structural color application of the 'Bodhisattva Padmapani' mural from Ajanta Cave 1. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Bodhisattva stands in a graceful tribhanga pose, holding a blue lotus. The composition utilizes rhythmic, sweeping contour lines and subtle tonal shading to build voluminous, three-dimensional form. His downcast eyes and serene expression project profound spiritual compassion, anchoring the chaotic, crowded narrative surrounding him.
